title: Constructible finite-coefficient sheaves on an oriented product
statement: Let $a:X\to S$ and $b:Y\to S$ be morphisms of schemes, and let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Put $P=X_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}Y_{\mathrm{Et}}$, the left oriented product of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. A sheaf $F$ of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over the constant ring sheaf $\Lambda_P$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] is called constructible if there are finite stratifications $X=\coprod_\alpha X_\alpha$, $Y=\coprod_\beta Y_\beta$ [def-constructible-stratification], with each stratum constructible as a subset [def-weil-constructible-subset], such that each restriction to $P_{\alpha\beta}=(X_\alpha)_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}(Y_\beta)_{\mathrm{Et}}$ is locally constant with finite $\Lambda$-module values. The map $P_{\alpha\beta}\to P$ is the morphism given by [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] from the projections, the stratum immersions, and the oriented $2$-morphism. Restriction is inverse image along that map. Here locally constant with finite values means that there is a covering family $(U_i)$ of the final object of $P_{\alpha\beta}$ such that on the slice topos $P_{\alpha\beta}/U_i$ the restricted sheaf is isomorphic to the constant sheaf $\underline{M_i}$ for a $\Lambda$-module $M_i$ finite as a set. For $Y=S$ and $b=1_S$, this defines constructibility on the vanishing topos $V_a$ [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles].

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q37-1980a5273 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: The definition is correct and matches Lu-Zheng (arXiv:1712.10216v7). I read the source from the pdftotext copy left at /tmp/q28lz/lz.txt, because literature/ has no copy and the network is blocked. The definition follows Theorem 4.27 at the top of printed p. 38. The general X <-x_S Y version is in section 1, after Corollary 1.26, on p. 12. The node takes finite Lambda, a specialization of the source's Noetherian Lambda; all three citers use finite Lambda, and for finite Lambda finitely generated stalks are finite stalks. The partitions match the source's finite disjoint constructible locally closed partitions: def-constructible-stratification plus constructible strata. The map P_ab -> P comes from lem-trf-oriented-product-universal applied to (iota_a p1, iota_b p2, tau_ab), and that lemma's hypotheses hold for small etale sites. The case Y=S, b=1_S is V_a of def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles. The node's 'locally constant with finite values' is equivalent to the source's two conditions together. Node to source: every point of P factors through some P_ab, so stalks are finite. Source to node: coherent oriented products have enough points (Lu-Zheng Lemma 1.3). I tested a point base, empty X, a strictly henselian trait whose strata give empty oriented strata, and the constant sheaf Lambda^(N), which is correctly excluded. No duplicate exists in the DAG or in any blueprint snapshot, so same_as [] is right. The existing locally-constant nodes cover only a scheme's etale site, so the inline definition is justified. There are no new nodes, no tool_uses and no SGA citation. Fix: source.place gave p. 37 and cited an Orgogozo 'author draft, section 8.1/Thm 7.1' that cannot be checked. I replaced it with the verified Lu-Zheng places (p. 38 after Thm 4.27, and p. 12 after Cor. 1.26) and Lu-Zheng's own attribution to [O, section 9.1].
